summary: Kuwait blames Iran for drones that killed two Italians, the EU fails to agree a budget, Kim Jong Un vows more nukes, Kushner presses Israel and SpaceX wins a huge satellite licence.

topics.heading: Kuwait says Iranian drones killed two Italian technicians; Iran denies it
topics.summary: Kuwait says it shot down Iranian drones over a military site and falling debris killed two Italian air-defence technicians.[^1] Iran's foreign minister denies Iran was behind it, and the EU's Ursula von der Leyen called for more pressure on Tehran.[^1][^2]

lead.title: Israeli strikes kill 10 in Gaza as Iranian drones kill 2 Italians in Kuwait, and other Mideast news

alsoReported.title: Live Updates: Iran accused of deadly drone attack in Kuwait that sparks EU call to step up pressure on Tehran

article: Kuwait is a small Gulf state that hosts US forces and has been caught up in the war between the US and Iran, which has run, with pauses, since February. On Thursday, Kuwait's defence ministry said it intercepted several Iranian drones aimed at what it called a vital site. Falling fragments killed two Italians and injured a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani.[^1][^2] Italy's foreign ministry says the two men were air-defence technicians working for a defence contractor.[^1]

Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, denied that Iran carried out the attack, and Iran's embassy in Rome said it "categorically rejects" the claim while offering condolences.[^1][^2] Kuwait has not published evidence beyond its statement.

Europe reacted quickly because Europeans died. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said "we must step up pressure on Iran" and that Gulf security matters to everyone.[^2] The same day, Saudi Arabia said an attack on its Jazan refinery killed a Nepali worker, and the Houthis, Iran's allies in Yemen, said they had fired at the Saudi ports of Jeddah and Jazan; Saudi forces say they shot the missiles and a drone down.[^1][^2]

Shipping keeps shrinking. Two more tankers were hit near the Strait of Hormuz; Iran's Revolutionary Guard says they hit mines while sailing without its permission, which AP could not verify.[^1] Data firm Kpler, cited by CBS, says weekly ship crossings fell from 217 to 147 in November, and tanker crossings are about a fifth of the pre-war level.[^2]

My read: the war is spreading sideways, to Kuwait, Saudi ports and Yemen, rather than escalating at its centre. Watch whether European countries move from statements to new sanctions, and whether Italy changes its role in Gulf air defence.
topics.differences: Kuwait says the drones were Iranian and killed two Italians; Iran's foreign minister and its embassy in Rome deny Iran was involved.[^1][^2] On the tankers, Iran's Revolutionary Guard says they hit mines; the UK maritime agency reported unknown projectiles.[^1]

topics.heading: EU summit ends without a budget deal; 24 countries back a €45B loan for Ukraine
topics.summary: A 14-hour EU summit failed to agree a 2028-2034 budget, and a planned second day was cancelled.[^3][^5] Twenty-four of 27 countries back a new loan of up to €45 billion for Ukraine in 2027; Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia stay out.[^3]

lead.title: EU Leaders Fail to Agree Long-Term Budget, Push Decisions to December

alsoReported.title: EU budget and Ukraine aid headed for collision at turbulent summit

article: Every seven years the EU's 27 governments must agree, unanimously, on a long-term budget. Council President António Costa proposed about €1.78 trillion for 2028-2034, roughly €200 billion less than the European Commission's plan.[^3] Leaders met in Brussels on Thursday, talked for about 14 hours and went home without a deal; Costa said they had found the outline of a "landing zone" for December.[^5]

The split is old and familiar. Seven net payers, including Germany, the Netherlands and Austria, want a smaller budget. Seventeen "Friends of Cohesion", mostly poorer members, refuse further cuts to farm and regional money.[^3] France's Emmanuel Macron insists French farmers lose nothing, and Italy's Giorgia Meloni said the sides were "light years" apart.[^5]

Ukraine is tied in. Ukraine faces a 2027 budget gap of about €70 billion. The Commission proposes a loan of up to €45 billion, €25 billion for the military and €20 billion for the budget, raised by EU borrowing and repaid only if Ukraine receives war reparations from Russia.[^3][^4] Twenty-four states back it. Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia are out, and Bulgaria joins only the civilian part.[^3] Germany's Friedrich Merz had threatened to veto the budget unless all 27 help Ukraine; Slovakia's Robert Fico called that "blackmail".[^4]
Leaders also recommended Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde as head of the European Central Bank in February.[^3]

What next: the next summit is December 17-18, the last before Macron's end-of-year deadline, though several leaders say they do not feel bound by it.[^3][^5] My read: the Ukraine loan is more likely to move in December than the full budget.
topics.differences: Net payers led by Germany say the budget must shrink further; France and the cohesion countries say the cuts already go too far.[^3][^5] Germany wants all 27 to fund Ukraine; Slovakia calls that pressure blackmail.[^4]

topics.heading: Kim Jong Un tours nuclear-fuel factories and calls for more weapons
topics.summary: North Korean state media says Kim inspected two factories making nuclear material and called for more nuclear weapons, including small battlefield ones.[^6] It came days after he ignored Donald Trump's offer to meet.[^6]

lead.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture

article: North Korea has built nuclear weapons for two decades despite UN sanctions. On Thursday its state news agency, KCNA, said leader Kim Jong Un had inspected two factories producing nuclear material, one newly opened and one being expanded, plus a research institute.[^6] Photos showed centrifuges, machines that enrich uranium, and what appeared to be warheads.[^6] North Korea did not say where the sites are.

Kim said the country must respond to nuclear threats around the Korean peninsula. He accused the US of helping allies get nuclear-powered submarines, and called low-yield battlefield nuclear weapons urgent, naming South Korea as the "most dangerous enemy state".[^6] South Korea's defence ministry said it takes those remarks seriously.[^6] Last week the head of the UN nuclear watchdog, Rafael Grossi, said North Korea is expanding its main enrichment plant at Yongbyon.[^6]

The timing matters. Trump offered to meet Kim during his recent Asia trip; there was no meeting and no public reply. Trump now says Kim "didn't ignore" him and that a meeting will come.[^6] A South Korean analyst told AP that Kim is showing off his arsenal and rejecting any talks on giving it up, possibly ahead of a party conference at year's end.[^6]
My read: North Korea is signalling that its weapons are not up for negotiation, while leaving room for talks on other terms. Watch the year-end party meeting for new weapons goals.

topics.heading: Kushner says Israel must drop its 'wartime mindset' as Gaza strikes continue
topics.summary: US envoy Jared Kushner said Israel should move from a "wartime mindset" to economic deals, and that the Gaza plan's next steps have not happened yet.[^7][^8] Gaza hospital officials say Israeli strikes killed 10 people overnight into Thursday.[^1]

lead.title: Kushner urges Israel to shed 'wartime mindset,' backs Gaza peace plan

alsoReported.title: US special envoy Jared Kushner urges Israel to shift from "wartime mindset" to economic diplomacy

article: Since a ceasefire took hold in Gaza in October 2025, the US-led Board of Peace has been trying to carry out Donald Trump's 20-point plan: Hamas gives up its weapons, Israeli troops pull back in phases, and a temporary Palestinian technocratic government runs Gaza.[^7] Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law and special envoy, is one of the plan's main authors.

In a podcast interview published Wednesday, Kushner said Israel needs to leave its "wartime mindset" and focus on economic diplomacy, such as data centres and energy projects with Egypt in Sinai.[^7][^8] He said neither Israeli withdrawal nor Hamas disarmament has happened yet, and that if they do not, Hamas stays in control or the UN or the Palestinian Authority takes over.[^7] He said Netanyahu signed the deal but "doesn't always make things easy", and that Israel's election and coalition talks have slowed the plan.[^7][^8] He also called the Palestinian Authority corrupt and Hamas a terrorist group.[^8]

On the ground, Gaza hospital officials told AP that Israeli strikes and a shooting killed 10 Palestinians overnight into Thursday. Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz say the army killed Khaled Abu Nada, whom they describe as a Hamas official for economic and education affairs.[^1] Gaza's health ministry, which does not separate civilians from fighters, says at least 74,746 Palestinians have died in the war.[^1]

Why it matters: Kushner's comments are some of the clearest public pressure from the Trump team on Netanyahu. Watch who forms Israel's next government; Kushner said any prime minister will have to make Gaza a priority.[^8]
topics.differences: Kushner says Israel's election and Netanyahu's caution have slowed the plan.[^7] Israel's government says its strikes target Hamas officials, while Gaza health officials report the dead without separating civilians from fighters.[^1]

topics.heading: US regulator lets SpaceX launch up to a million AI data-centre satellites
topics.summary: The FCC approved SpaceX's "Starmind" plan for up to 1,000,000 satellites that would run AI computing in orbit.[^9] Astronomers and rival satellite firms objected, and experts doubt the full number will ever fly.[^9][^10]

lead.title: US grants SpaceX approval for 1 million space data centres

alsoReported.title: FCC green lights SpaceX's plan to launch 1 million 'Starmind' data center satellites

article: AI needs huge amounts of computing power, electricity and cooling. Elon Musk's SpaceX argues some of that can move to space, where sunlight is constant. On Wednesday the US Federal Communications Commission, which licenses satellites, approved its Starmind network of up to one million orbiting "compute modules". FCC chair Brendan Carr called it a bold new frontier.[^9]

For scale, about 17,000 satellites exist in total today.[^9] The licence sets deadlines: a first satellite by 2033, half the network by 2038 and all of it by 2040.[^10] Musk says launches could start in late 2027 and ramp up in 2028 and 2029; SpaceX is building the satellites with Nvidia.[^10] Each would be large, with a wingspan of about 75 metres.[^10]

Critics raised several worries. The American Astronomical Society said it is "gravely concerned" about effects on astronomy, since bright satellites streak across telescope images. Rival operators Amazon Leo and Viasat raised radio interference, and Amazon argued SpaceX would never deploy all of them. The FCC rejected their petitions, but delayed a decision on how SpaceX would dispose of satellites in high orbits.[^9][^10]

My read: a licence is permission, not proof. Companies often ask for more satellites than they launch: SpaceX sought 42,000 Starlink satellites and has just over 11,000 up.[^9] The bigger signal is that governments now treat AI computing as infrastructure worth crowding orbit for.
topics.differences: The FCC says its rules address interference and astronomy concerns; the American Astronomical Society says the licence lacks formal coordination requirements.[^10]

question.text: Kuwait says Iranian drones killed two Italians and Iran denies it; Iran says tankers hit mines while others report unknown projectiles. When the parties to a war contradict each other, what kind of evidence would actually change your mind, and who could provide it?

read.title: FCC green lights SpaceX's plan to launch 1 million 'Starmind' data center satellites
read.summary: A detailed look at what the FCC approved for SpaceX's orbital AI network: deadlines, satellite size, links, debris rules, and the objections from astronomers and rival operators.
